topic: Area B: Personal and Social Life
subject: spanish

items.q: What is the Spanish word for 'mobile phone' (in Spain)?
items.misconception: El celular (which is used in Latin America).
items.why: Vocabulary varies by region. Spain: móvil, ordenador (computer), coche (car). Latin America: celular, computadora, carro/auto. Students mix these. Examiners accept both, but consistency matters. Móvil is most common in GCSE/A-level.
Students apply English pronunciation. Spanish H is ALWAYS silent. 'Hola' is 'OH-lah', not 'HO-lah'. (The breathy sound students associate with H comes from j or g+e/i in Spanish.)

items.q: How do you say 'I wash myself' in Spanish?
items.why: Students translate word-for-word. Spanish reflexive verbs use SPECIAL PRONOUNS before the verb: me, te, se, nos, os, se. The reflexive pronoun does the work English does with 'myself/yourself'.
The answer examiners want is: Me gusta el español.. “Me gusto el español.” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: Which sentence means 'Maths is more difficult than English'?
items.correct: Las matemáticas son más difíciles que el inglés.
items.misconception: Las matemáticas es más difícil que el inglés.
items.random_wrong: Las matemáticas son menos difíciles que el inglés.
items.why: It's Las matemáticas son más difíciles que el inglés.. “Las matemáticas es más difícil que el inglés.” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: How many subject pronouns does Spanish have (yo, tú, él/ella/usted, nosotros, vosotros, ellos/ellas/ustedes)?
items.why: The real figure is 6 pronouns. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
